pr_title: tests: drivers: can: timing: test that calculated timings can be set
pr_body:
This patch set adds the following CAN timing test cases:
- tests: drivers: can: timing: test that calculated timings can be set
- tests: drivers: can: timing: test min/max timing can be set

The addition of these test cases revealed a few bugs, for which fixes are included:
- drivers: can: mcan: allow sjw == CAN_SJW_NO_CHANGE (Fixes: #44482)
- drivers: can: mcan: fix bounds check for data phase prescaler (Fixes: #44483)
- drivers: can: mcp2515: correct min/max timing values (Fixes: #44484)

Furthermore, the handler for `can_set_timing()` is changes to validate all parameters and copy them before calling the implementation.

The tested sample point locations for bitrates >= 800kbit/s have been modified to match those uses in the Linux kernel CAN layer as these seem to be much more likely to be met with 100% accuracy by a wide range of CAN controllers. I will follow up with a PR for changing the default sample point locations used by `can_set_bitrate()`.
pr_comments:
> Thanks for catching those mcp2515 off by one (bit) errors....

Welcome.

> Was this marked draft by purpose? Looks small and self contained enough to be good enough as is?

Yes, it was converted to draft on purpose. I needed to get a minor change in. It is ready for review now.
Rebased to fix an issue with passing non-NULL `timing_data_copy` even if user passed NULL `timing_data`.

issue_context.title: drivers: can: mcp2515: The MCP2515 driver uses wrong timing limits
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
- The MCP2515 requires phase segment 2 to be at least 2 time quanta, but the driver allows `phase_seg2` to be 0x01.
- The MCP2515 prescaler has a 6 bit register, allowing for real-world prescaler values between 1 and 64, but the driver limits this to 0x20.

**Expected behavior**
Minimal `phase_seg2` should be 0x02 and maximum `prescaler` should be 0x40.

**Impact**
Prevents users (and test cases) to set certain timing. Allows for calculating timing values not valid for the device.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Ubuntu Linux v20.04 LTS
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK v0.14.0
 - Commit SHA: e04172fcef2c69992884246dcad3aa3727d56cd6

the test case is supposed to try to set `timing`, not `min_timing`. 
I guess `min_timing` is used in the can-fd case to avoid setting the same timing configuration for both data and regular timings.

@karstenkoenig Exactly. We cannot set the same timing for both the arbitration and data phase as they may have different limits. Therefore, the data phase timing test simply uses the minimum timing allowed by the driver for the arbitration phase (at this point, that was already validated by another test case).
